page: Amazon Web Services r6gd.8xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. It features 32 dedicated physical cores on the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Additionally, it includes 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps, managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark results place the r6gd.8xlarge in the average tier for most multi-core and memory operations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test scored 48584.58, and the Geekbench multi-core score reached 11391.0. Memory bandwidth tests show 1894.04 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 150.22 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 933.0 and a poor bzip3 single-threaded decompression speed of 6.62 GB/sec. Redis SET operations achieved 38.98 million operations per second, and Passmark database operations scored 19957.42.

The ARM64 architecture and dedicated core allocation offer a cost-efficient alternative to traditional x86 memory-optimized instances, delivering high resource density without hyperthreading overhead. With its large memory footprint and fast local NVMe SSD storage, this instance is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, caching layers like Redis, and static web serving. It is less optimal for single-threaded compute tasks or workloads requiring advanced x86 vector instructions.
